source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15 ("Apathy in Rural Districts") ("Armagh Rural: No Nominations in Fourteen Divisions")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name and label checked against the page image; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the rural district council (31 divisions), 1930: nominations received by William Calvert, clerk of Armagh Union, 29 April 1930. There were no contests; in 14 divisions there were no nominations and the retiring members were declared re-elected. Returned unopposed. So printed; the same name (as Gibson) is printed for Armaghbrague, and J. J. W. Dunlop held Annaghmore in 1924 and 1927, so this entry may be a misprint.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the paper prints 'John V. Gilbson' for Annaghmore (kept in Name_As_Printed) and 'John V. Gibson' for Armaghbrague on the next line; he is recorded as John V. Gibson. The page link was added to the citation.
